tasks.short: Check supplier and agency invoices, resolve exceptions, and prepare approved payments in AFAS.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives in Outlook or an agency portal, or a payment run is due.
steps: Find the invoice and check supplier details, amounts, VAT and possible duplicates.
Compare charges with approved orders, service evidence or agency hours and agreed rates.
Check the bookkeeper's coding and resolve differences with the site or agency.
Confirm approval and prepare the payment selection in AFAS.
Send the batch for authorised release in Rabobank and retain supporting records.
drudgery: Copying invoice details between documents and AFAS.
Comparing agency hours and rates line by line.
Chasing missing approvals and checking the same invoice twice.
today.time_sinks: Likely concentrated in agency invoice differences, missing service evidence and approval chasing; actual exception rates need measurement.

lenses.faster: Import structured invoices and agency exports, then check totals, duplicates, coding and approvals with rules. Use document extraction only where structured data is unavailable.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice arrival starts validation and routes discrepancies to the right owner. A scheduled run prepares the approved payment selection, with bank release still requiring authorised people.
lenses.ambitious: Check every agency invoice against approved hours and negotiated rates across all three sites. Report recurring overcharges and missing evidence before they delay the close.
lenses.joy: Remove rekeying and repeated approval chasing. Keep supplier problem solving and finding the cause of persistent billing errors.
lenses.options: Prepare payment selections for due dates, early-payment discounts and cash constraints. Show the cash effect and overdue obligations for each choice.
lenses.altitude: Own the invoice control rules, exception thresholds and supplier quality measures. Improve the share processed without accountant intervention.
reach: Bookkeeper: resolve complex invoice matching and coding exceptions.
Controller: maintain supplier and payment control evidence.
FP&A Analyst: provide upcoming supplier and agency cash requirements.

tasks.human_edge: Judge disputed services, unusual VAT treatment and suspected fraud; maintain independent supplier bank verification and payment authorisation.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules handle arithmetic, matching and routing; an llm_step can extract unstructured descriptions. Approval is required before the payment batch counts as released, so the whole task remains gated.

in_practice.trigger: New invoice received or a scheduled payment preparation window opens.
steps: Capture the invoice with a unique identifier; import structured fields or extract document fields with source references.
Validate totals, VAT codes, duplicates and supplier details against approved AFAS master data.
Match charges to approved orders, service evidence or agency hours and rates; hold missing or ambiguous matches.
Route exceptions and approvals, then prepare the eligible payment selection in AFAS.
After authorised bank release, record batch identifiers and reconcile the resulting bank movements.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant resolves exceptions; budget owners approve expenditure; authorised bank signatories release the batch under the existing mandate. The workflow cannot change supplier bank accounts.
systems: Proposed Power Automate workflow and optional AI Builder extraction
data_needed: Supplier master data and independently verified bank details.
Invoices, credit notes, payment terms and existing approvals.
Approved service or receiving evidence.
Agency hours, orders, rate agreements and authorised adjustments.
Coding rules, VAT rules and payment authority limits.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS transaction and payment references plus a restricted SharePoint control register recording source documents, rule versions, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: AI Builder can extract invoice fields and confidence scores inside a Power Automate flow; this supports capture, not payment correctness.
Power Automate supports human approval workflows; the proposed AFAS and Rabobank integration still needs local validation.
The estimated saving and speedup assume most invoices have usable matching evidence and exceptions remain a minority.

risks: Correct extraction can still match the wrong invoice, hours record or supplier.
Duplicate imports or retries can create duplicate liabilities without unique identifiers and posting checks.
Invoice text could contain instructions that must never override control rules or approved bank details.
Agency documents can contain personal data; use only necessary fields with restricted access.
Automating preparation must preserve separation between supplier maintenance, invoice approval and bank release.
research_questions: What proportion of the accountant's invoice time concerns clean invoices versus genuine disputes?
Can all three agencies export approved hours, negotiated rates and invoice lines with stable matching identifiers?
Which AFAS import and approval functions are enabled, and can they preserve the current payment controls?
Does a shadow run reduce handling time without increasing duplicate, VAT or payment errors?

tasks.short: Check that the accounts and financial reports are complete, accurate and ready for the close.

today.trigger: A periodic review, draft month-end report or reporting deadline requires a checked set of accounts.
steps: Export the AFAS trial balance, ledger movements and relevant subledgers.
Check report totals and investigate missing, unusual or incorrectly classified entries.
Compare balances and movements with prior periods and supporting schedules.
Check treatment against the company's accounting policies and reporting requirements.
Document findings, arrange corrections and submit the checked report to the Controller.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same control totals and variance tables.
Tracing report figures back to ledger entries.
Collecting support already supplied for another close check.
today.time_sinks: Repeated exports, inconsistent report versions and investigation of unexplained movements; nightly Power BI data can lag late close entries.

lenses.faster: Run repeatable completeness, tie-out and variance checks on a timestamped AFAS snapshot. Draft explanations from linked evidence, leaving the accountant to assess exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: Each successful extract starts the checks and updates the exception register. Failed or incomplete extracts stop the run instead of producing a clean report.
lenses.ambitious: Review transactions throughout the month and show emerging problems by Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Give FP&A earlier warning of agency cost, payroll and supplier accrual gaps.
lenses.joy: Remove rebuilding spreadsheets and hunting for source lines. Keep the work of explaining what changed and whether the business can trust the result.
lenses.options: Show alternative materiality thresholds and provisional treatments for unresolved items. Quantify their effects on profit, balance sheet and the forecast input.
lenses.altitude: Design the checks that make reports dependable and investigate why they fail. Measure late corrections and audit adjustments rather than how many reports were checked.
reach: Controller: maintain the close quality dashboard and supporting evidence.
FP&A Analyst: validate actuals and explain accounting effects before forecast updates.
Bookkeeper: identify recurring posting errors and improve upstream checks.

tasks.human_edge: Assess substance, materiality, estimates and accounting treatment; challenge plausible explanations and accept responsibility for the reviewed report.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic checks can cover the ledger and assemble evidence, while a model drafts commentary. Accuracy, completeness and conformity of the final report still require accountable review.

in_practice.trigger: A validated AFAS extract is available or a draft close report is submitted.
steps: Freeze a dated snapshot and verify record counts, control totals and reporting scope.
Run approved checks for subledger agreement, missing dimensions, unusual movements and cut-off indicators.
Create exceptions with ledger references, supporting documents and quantified report effects.
Draft commentary using only retrieved evidence, marking unsupported explanations as unresolved.
Route corrections and refresh the checks before the accountant and Controller approve the report.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant reviews material findings and explanations; Controller approves the final close report. Model commentary cannot clear an exception or certify compliance.
systems: AFAS Profit extracts or authorised GetConnectors
Proposed controlled analysis workflow and approved language model
data_needed: Complete trial balance, ledger and subledgers from the same snapshot.
Approved accounting policies, report mappings and materiality thresholds.
Prior-period balances and supporting schedules.
Payroll control totals validated by the Payroll Specialist.
Agency hours and supplier service evidence relevant to cut-off.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint close evidence library, with snapshot identifiers, check results, report versions, corrections and sign-offs linked to AFAS entries.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors provide a documented route to retrieve configured datasets; coverage and permissions must be checked locally.
Rules can test report tie-outs and flag movements, but a balanced ledger alone does not prove completeness or correct accounting treatment.
The saving and speedup estimates assume stable report mappings and accessible supporting schedules.

risks: Checks can pass while an unrecorded obligation remains absent from every source.
Nightly Power BI figures may exclude entries posted during the close.
A model may invent a convincing explanation for a variance.
Incorrect materiality thresholds can suppress important errors.
Payroll evidence must exclude medical absence details and unnecessary employee identifiers.
research_questions: Which review checks caused actual corrections or audit adjustments in the last six closes?
Can ledger, subledger and supporting schedules be captured with a consistent cut-off?
What share of findings can be resolved from evidence rather than interviews and judgement?
Does a shadow review detect known errors while keeping false alerts manageable?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, supplier, customer and payroll control accounts, and explain outstanding differences.

today.trigger: A bank statement arrives, a control account differs from its supporting records, or the close timetable requires reconciliation.
steps: Collect AFAS balances, bank statements and supporting subledger or payroll totals.
Match transactions by reference, amount and date in AFAS or Excel.
Separate timing differences from missing, duplicate or incorrect entries.
Investigate unmatched items with the bookkeepers, Payroll Specialist or agency.
Prepare corrections and document the remaining differences for review.
drudgery: Repeating lookups across large transaction exports.
Rolling forward unchanged outstanding items.
Reconstructing the history of an old difference.
today.time_sinks: Ambiguous references, combined payments, credits and old differences with weak ownership; routine matching should first be assessed against existing AFAS functions.

lenses.faster: Refresh matching rules and roll forward open items automatically. Show only unmatched or changed differences, with their source records and previous investigation.
lenses.autonomous: New statements and extracts trigger exact matching and exception preparation. Ambiguous combinations remain proposals until a person confirms them.
lenses.ambitious: Reconcile key control accounts daily and assign every difference an owner and age. Catch agency and payroll interface problems before month-end.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive matching and repeated explanations of the same outstanding item. Keep investigating the difficult differences and fixing their source.
lenses.options: For ambiguous payments, show a few candidate matches with exact sums and supporting references. Explain why each candidate fits and what evidence is missing.
lenses.altitude: Manage reconciliation coverage, unmatched-item ageing and recurring causes. Improve the rules and upstream references rather than matching every line.
reach: Bookkeeper: improve payment allocation and reference quality.
Credit and Collections Officer: identify receipts awaiting customer allocation.
Payroll Specialist: investigate differences between payroll journals, liabilities and payments.

tasks.human_edge: Resolve ambiguous allocations, decide whether an item is a timing difference or error, and authorise corrections or write-offs.
tasks.pattern_why: Most matching and roll-forward work uses structured records and checkable arithmetic. AI can help build the rules; production matching does not need a model, and final reconciliation acceptance remains human.

in_practice.trigger: A new bank statement or validated control-account extract becomes available.
steps: Validate source completeness and reconcile opening balance plus movements to closing balance.
Apply exact reference and amount matches, preventing any transaction from being used twice.
Apply approved grouping rules and prepare ambiguous matches separately.
Carry forward unresolved differences with owner, age and source links.
Obtain review of material differences and route corrections through the journal approval process.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves ambiguous matches and certifies material reconciliations; an independent reviewer approves corrections and write-offs according to authority limits.
systems: Excel Power Query or a proposed deterministic matching service
data_needed: Bank movements and statement opening and closing balances.
AFAS ledger and subledger transactions with stable identifiers.
Payroll journal and payment control totals.
Approved matching rules, tolerances and account owners.
Previous reconciliations and unresolved-item histories.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reconciliation register containing matched transaction identifiers, rule versions, unresolved items, approvals and links to AFAS corrections.

evidence.claim: Power Query supports merging tables using join types, providing a component for exact matching and unmatched-item lists.
Deterministic matching can handle exact references and approved groupings; ambiguous allocations still need judgement.
The saving and speedup estimates assume a substantial residual volume of repetitive matching beyond existing AFAS automation.

risks: Equal amounts can produce false matches without reliable references.
Grouping rules can conceal duplicate payments or missing transactions.
A reconciliation can appear complete if both compared datasets omit the same records.
Automatic tolerances can accumulate material differences.
Gains may be small if AFAS already handles nearly all straightforward matches.
research_questions: How much matching is already automatic in AFAS, and what remains for the accountants?
What proportion of unmatched items has reliable references or repeatable grouping rules?
Can a trial reproduce approved historical reconciliations without false matches or reused transactions?
Are persistent differences caused by matching effort or by unresolved business disputes?

tasks.short: Review how AFAS and our accounting procedures work, and find control gaps and wasted effort.

today.trigger: A recurring error, audit finding, process change or scheduled control review raises a concern.
steps: Collect accounting procedures, configuration evidence, permissions and transaction samples.
Walk through the process with bookkeepers and relevant site staff.
Test whether approvals, coding, cut-off and records operate as intended.
Compare actual practice with company policies and accepted accounting procedures.
Recommend improvements and agree owners and follow-up checks.
drudgery: Collecting the same configuration screenshots and evidence.
Manually assembling transaction samples.
Comparing procedures with scattered records.
today.time_sinks: Obtaining reliable evidence and understanding workarounds across three sites; documenting a process does not establish that its controls work.

lenses.faster: Assemble evidence and draft a control comparison before the review. Test complete transaction populations where rules are explicit instead of manually selecting every sample.
lenses.autonomous: Scheduled tests flag missing approvals, late postings and repeated overrides where the required logs exist. They prepare findings without declaring a process effective.
lenses.ambitious: Review controls across all three sites continuously and measure whether fixes reduce rework and close delays. Include exceptions that never became audit adjustments.
lenses.joy: Remove screenshot gathering and repetitive evidence indexing. Keep staff interviews, understanding workarounds and designing practical fixes.
lenses.options: Compare configuration changes, simpler procedures and extra controls by cost, workload and expected risk reduction. Include a measured pilot option.
lenses.altitude: Become the designer and tester of accounting controls. Use evidence to improve the process rather than repeatedly inspect isolated transactions.
reach: Controller: maintain the accounting control register and remediation evidence.
Bookkeeper: redesign recurring approval and posting problems.
Finance Director: prepare evidence-based priorities for finance process investment.

tasks.human_edge: Understand why staff bypass a procedure, judge whether a control is proportionate, and distinguish a tidy system from an effective one.
tasks.pattern_why: Tools can collect evidence, test explicit rules and draft findings. The accountant leads interviews, evaluates accounting suitability and agrees changes with the people responsible.

in_practice.trigger: A control review is scheduled or repeated exceptions cross an agreed threshold.
steps: Define the process scope, expected controls and evidence required.
Retrieve authorised transaction events, configuration records and policy versions.
Run explicit control tests and assemble examples of failures or bottlenecks.
Draft findings with source links and alternative remedies.
Validate findings through walkthroughs, agree actions and test whether the implemented change works.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant validates every finding and recommendation; Controller approves control design, and system owners approve configuration changes.
systems: Optional Power Automate Process Mining if suitable event logs and licences exist
Approved language model for evidence-based drafts
data_needed: Versioned accounting procedures and approved control objectives.
Transaction events with case identifiers, activity names and timestamps.
Approval, override and configuration histories where available.
Authorised access-role evidence.
Audit findings, close delays and rework records.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint control register with evidence references, test definitions, validated findings, action owners and follow-up results.

evidence.claim: Power Automate Process Mining can use event data to map processes, compare paths and expose bottlenecks; it requires suitable data and licensing.
Population checks and evidence-based drafts can shorten preparation, while interviews and control judgements remain human work.
The saving and speedup estimates assume usable process evidence without substantial reconstruction.

risks: Missing event logs can make a process look simpler or more compliant than it is.
A model may confuse written policy with observed practice.
Removing an apparently redundant step can weaken separation of duties.
Employee-level monitoring would require separate consideration of AVG/GDPR and OR involvement; use process-level evidence for this proposal.
The review cannot replace independent external audit assurance.
research_questions: Do AFAS and existing approval records contain enough event history to reconstruct the chosen process?
Which recent control findings required staff interviews rather than data analysis?
Can automated tests reproduce known control failures without excessive false alerts?
Would evidence preparation save more time than collecting and maintaining the required logs?

tasks.short: Prepare accruals, prepayments and corrections so the month reflects the costs and income it should.

today.trigger: Month-end requires routine adjustments, or a reconciliation or review identifies an error.
steps: Collect invoices, schedules, payroll totals and evidence of services delivered.
Calculate accruals, prepayments, allocations and any required reversals in Excel.
Choose ledger accounts, site dimensions, dates and tax treatment where relevant.
Prepare the journal and supporting explanation for review.
Post approved entries in AFAS and check balances and reversal dates.
drudgery: Copying last month's journal and replacing amounts.
Recalculating fixed schedules and checking debits equal credits.
Tracking reversals and gathering support repeatedly.
today.time_sinks: Late agency hours and invoices, changing estimates and rebuilding recurring schedules; judgement-heavy provisions take longer than routine journals.

lenses.faster: Calculate recurring journals from approved schedules and prepare an AFAS import with linked support. Remove manual copying, balancing and reversal tracking.
lenses.autonomous: The close calendar triggers journal preparation when source data passes completeness checks. Missing hours or invoices create exceptions instead of guessed amounts.
lenses.ambitious: Refresh provisional agency and other service accruals weekly so FP&A sees likely costs earlier. Compare each estimate with its eventual invoice and improve the method.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive journal construction and reversal administration. Keep deciding what belongs in the period and explaining meaningful estimate changes.
lenses.options: For uncertain accruals, show documented low, central and high estimates and their profit effects. Separate observed quantities from assumptions.
lenses.altitude: Own adjustment policies, schedules and estimate quality. Monitor late adjustments and repeated accrual errors instead of rebuilding every journal.
reach: Controller: manage adjustment controls and close readiness.
FP&A Analyst: provide provisional actuals and accrual uncertainty.
Payroll Specialist: reconcile approved payroll journals to finance control accounts.

tasks.human_edge: Choose accounting treatment and reasonable estimates, especially provisions, disputed charges and unusual corrections.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic software handles schedule calculations, balanced entries and reversals. The accountant and reviewer approve the source basis and treatment before any adjustment is posted.

in_practice.trigger: A close milestone arrives or an approved correction request is raised.
steps: Load versioned schedules and approved source quantities, rates and control totals.
Calculate adjustments using approved formulas and flag missing inputs or unusual changes.
Prepare balanced journal lines with site coding, support, reversal instructions and a unique journal key.
Present amounts and assumptions for accountant review and independent approval.
Post through an authorised AFAS interface, verify the result and register any scheduled reversal.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant validates assumptions and treatment; Controller or another authorised reviewer approves posting. Payroll rules and CAO interpretations remain with the Payroll Specialist.
systems: Excel or proposed deterministic schedule service
data_needed: Approved accrual, prepayment and allocation schedules.
Agency hours, agreed rates, service periods and invoices already posted.
Validated payroll journal and liability totals.
Chart of accounts, site dimensions and open periods.
Posting authority limits and approved reversal policy.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS journal references plus a restricted SharePoint adjustment register with calculation inputs, formula versions, assumptions, approvals and reversal status.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents the FiEntries UpdateConnector for adding financial entries; local permissions and supported fields require validation.
Approved schedules can generate repeatable journals, while uncertain estimates and novel accounting treatment still need review.
The saving and speedup estimates assume recurring schedules account for most journal preparation effort.

risks: A journal can balance while using the wrong period, site or accounting treatment.
An accrual can duplicate an invoice posted after the source snapshot.
Repeated workflow runs can duplicate entries without unique keys and post-verification.
Missing reversals can overstate later costs.
Agency rates and payroll totals can be outdated even when the formula is correct.
research_questions: What share of adjustments follows stable schedules versus new estimates or accounting judgements?
Are approved agency hours and validated payroll totals available before the close deadline?
Can AFAS posting and reversal handling be tested without duplicate entries or closed-period changes?
Do historical back-tests reproduce approved journals and reveal accrual estimate errors?

tasks.short: Coordinate the finance team's records, deadlines and handovers, and help people clear blocked work.

today.trigger: Daily processing needs coordination, a close deadline approaches or a record is missing.
steps: Check outstanding finance tasks, missing documents and close deadlines.
Agree priorities and ownership with bookkeepers and other contributors.
Request missing records and clarify how they should be filed or supplied.
Review completion evidence and resolve blockers or escalate them.
Update the close checklist and report readiness to the Controller.
drudgery: Sending repeated reminders for the same documents.
Maintaining status in several places.
Opening folders to check whether evidence has arrived.
today.time_sinks: Status chasing and unclear ownership; genuine capacity problems, coaching and conflicting deadlines require conversations.

lenses.faster: Use one evidence-linked checklist that updates from completed workflow steps. Prepare a short blocker list instead of collecting status through separate emails.
lenses.autonomous: Agreed deadlines trigger reminders and escalate missing evidence to the designated owner. Completion is recognised only when the required evidence or approval exists.
lenses.ambitious: Coordinate close readiness throughout the month across all three sites. Identify repeated handover failures and fix their cause before the next close.
lenses.joy: Remove reminder writing and status copying. Keep helping colleagues solve problems, coaching and agreeing sensible priorities.
lenses.options: Show alternative close sequences when a dependency is late, with the impact on completion and review capacity. Let the accountant agree changes with the team.
lenses.altitude: Design clear ownership, handovers and escalation rules. Spend time improving team reliability rather than maintaining the checklist.
reach: Controller: coordinate the operational close timetable and dependency status.
Bookkeeper: standardise evidence filing and handover requirements.
FP&A Analyst: coordinate the release of checked actuals for forecasting.

tasks.human_edge: Lead people, recognise overload, resolve disagreements and coach colleagues; formal supervision and performance decisions remain with the responsible manager.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic workflows can automate reminders and evidence status, but directing personnel requires judgement and relationships. The earlier automate label fits the administrative portion more strongly than the whole task.

in_practice.trigger: A close cycle opens, a deadline approaches or a required evidence item becomes overdue.
steps: Create the checklist from an approved template with agreed owners, dependencies and deadlines.
Update status from document receipt and approval events, checking evidence completeness.
Send reminders under agreed rules and collect blockers in one register.
Prepare a dependency summary and possible changes to the work sequence.
Accountant agrees priorities with colleagues and records decisions and escalations.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves priority changes, workload reallocations and escalations outside agreed rules. The workflow does not evaluate staff performance or make personnel decisions.
data_needed: Approved close checklist and dependency map.
Agreed task owners, deadlines and escalation contacts.
Required evidence definitions and document locations.
Approval and completion events.
Team-supplied blockers and availability.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close coordination register with evidence links, reminder history, blockers, agreed priority changes and completion approvals.

evidence.claim: Power Automate supports approval workflows that can be combined with Microsoft 365 task and document processes.
Evidence-linked status and reminders can reduce coordination administration, but cannot resolve workload conflicts or replace coaching.
The saving and speedup estimates assume status chasing accounts for a substantial part of this task.

risks: Document arrival can be mistaken for completion even when evidence is inadequate.
Excessive reminders can create noise and hide important blockers.
Incorrect dependencies can push work into the wrong sequence.
Using task data to score individuals or automatically allocate their work would need a separate OR, AVG/GDPR and EU AI Act assessment.
Automation may expose late work without addressing the underlying capacity shortage.
research_questions: How much time goes to status chasing versus coaching and resolving real blockers?
Can completed tasks be linked to reliable evidence rather than self-reported status alone?
Do contributors accept a shared checklist and agreed reminder rules?
Does a pilot shorten handovers and close delays without increasing reminder noise?

tasks.short: Maintain the chart of accounts and make sure entries use the right account and site.

today.trigger: A new transaction type needs coding, an account change is requested or a review finds inconsistent classification.
steps: Review the transaction and search existing accounts and coding guidance.
Determine the correct expense, asset, liability or revenue classification and site dimensions.
Propose a new or amended account if the existing chart cannot support the requirement.
Obtain approval and update AFAS configuration and reporting mappings.
Check subsequent entries and correct inconsistent coding.
drudgery: Searching old entries to infer coding precedent.
Repeating the same supplier and transaction classifications.
Checking several reporting mappings after an account change.
today.time_sinks: Unclear descriptions, inconsistent historical coding and downstream mapping changes; routine assignments and chart design are different kinds of work.

lenses.faster: Apply approved account and dimension rules to repeat transactions. For unfamiliar descriptions, suggest accounts with policy references and comparable reviewed entries.
lenses.autonomous: A new transaction triggers coding checks and flags invalid combinations. Requests for new accounts produce a proposal and mapping impact list for approval.
lenses.ambitious: Make site and cost-category coding consistent across the three locations. Identify where account detail prevents a useful agency, payroll or supplier cost forecast.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated searches for familiar coding and manual mapping comparisons. Keep designing a chart that explains the business clearly.
lenses.options: Show a few coding candidates for ambiguous transactions and compare keeping an existing account with creating a new one. Include effects on historical comparisons and reporting.
lenses.altitude: Own classification policy and chart governance. Improve rules and monitor coding quality rather than decide every routine line.
reach: Bookkeeper: maintain routine transaction coding rules.
Controller: govern chart changes and financial statement mappings.
FP&A Analyst: align account and site dimensions with forecast categories.

tasks.human_edge: Decide substance over wording, asset versus expense treatment and the appropriate reporting structure; approve new accounts and policy changes.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved rules handle familiar assignments, and an llm_step can propose classifications from descriptions. New accounts, ambiguous coding and reporting changes require approval before use.

in_practice.trigger: An unfamiliar transaction, invalid coding combination or chart-change request is detected.
steps: Retrieve the current chart, coding policy, valid site dimensions and reviewed examples.
Apply exact approved rules; propose alternatives for unfamiliar transactions with supporting references.
For chart changes, check duplicate accounts and identify affected reports and forecast mappings.
Route uncertain coding and configuration proposals to the accountant and Controller.
Apply approved changes through authorised AFAS configuration or import procedures and verify downstream mappings.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves ambiguous classification; Controller approves new accounts and reporting changes. Historical entries are changed only through a separately approved correction.
systems: Proposed rule engine and approved language model
data_needed: Current chart of accounts and account restrictions.
Approved accounting and VAT coding policies.
Valid site and cost dimensions.
Reviewed transaction examples and source descriptions.
Financial report and forecast mapping tables.
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint chart-change and coding-rule register, recording policy references, approvals, effective dates and affected AFAS and Power BI mappings.

evidence.claim: Rules can assign repeat transaction classes and validate dimensions; description-based suggestions need review for unfamiliar items.
Power Query table joins can help compare account mappings and identify missing or inconsistent mappings.
The saving and speedup estimates assume repeat coding dominates effort and chart changes remain occasional.

risks: Historical coding can contain errors that a model repeats.
Supplier-level rules can misclassify invoices covering several services or sites.
Uncontrolled account creation can fragment reporting and weaken comparability.
Changed mappings can silently alter prior-period Power BI reports.
Text descriptions alone may not establish asset recognition or correct VAT treatment.
research_questions: How much effort concerns recurring coding versus chart design and unusual accounting treatment?
Are coding policies and reviewed examples consistent enough to support reliable rules?
Can a trial classify held-out transactions without material account or site errors?
Can account changes be traced through every affected financial report and forecast mapping?

tasks.short: Improve and document our accounting workflows, AFAS interfaces and controls.

today.trigger: An error pattern, new reporting need, audit finding or operational change requires a system improvement.
steps: Describe the current workflow, problem and required accounting controls.
Agree requirements with bookkeepers, the Controller and system owners.
Design configuration, interface or spreadsheet changes and prepare test cases.
Test representative transactions and failure conditions before approval.
Implement the approved change, document it and support users.
drudgery: Writing similar specifications and user instructions repeatedly.
Building repetitive field mappings and spreadsheet transformations.
Collecting screenshots and maintaining scattered documentation.
today.time_sinks: Clarifying requirements, obtaining access, testing integrations and coordinating changes; generated code does not remove system-owner dependencies.

lenses.faster: Draft specifications, mappings, test data and instructions from approved requirements. Use AI coding assistance to build small deterministic checks and transformations for review.
lenses.autonomous: Approved regression checks run after changes or extracts and flag failures. Production configuration changes remain under the normal approval process.
lenses.ambitious: Build reusable finance interfaces and controls across all three sites instead of separate spreadsheet fixes. Prioritise changes that reduce close delays and improve trusted forecast inputs.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive documentation and mapping work. Keep solving accounting problems with colleagues and seeing a reliable process replace a workaround.
lenses.options: Compare AFAS configuration, an Excel transformation and a maintained integration by controls, effort, ownership and running cost. Prototype the most uncertain part before choosing.
lenses.altitude: Become the finance owner of accounting system design and acceptance criteria. Define what correct behaviour means and ensure every automation has an owner.
reach: Controller: design and verify finance controls in system changes.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: jointly govern payroll-to-finance data interfaces.
FP&A Analyst: improve actuals mappings and data quality for forecasting.
Bookkeeper: simplify invoice and posting workflows.

tasks.human_edge: Translate business needs into accounting controls, negotiate trade-offs and accept whether a change is fit for production.
tasks.pattern_why: AI helps draft designs, code and documentation, but the accountant leads requirements and acceptance. Approved production transformations should run as deterministic software with controlled releases.

in_practice.trigger: An approved finance improvement request enters the change backlog.
steps: Define the problem, measurable outcome, data scope and control requirements.
Draft solution options, interface mappings and operating instructions with source references.
Build the chosen configuration or transformation in a test environment using masked or synthetic data.
Test valid transactions, missing data, duplicate runs, access restrictions and failed posting recovery.
Obtain business and technical approval, release with a rollback method and verify production results.
Record the owner, support procedure and measured effect on close or processing performance.
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant accepts accounting behaviour; Controller approves control changes; authorised system owners approve and perform production release.
systems: AFAS test and production environments, if available
Proposed controlled code repository and automation runtime
data_needed: Approved requirements and current workflow descriptions.
AFAS connector schemas, permissions and configuration documentation.
Agency export formats and sample records.
Expected accounting results and control totals.
Existing access roles, release procedures and recovery requirements.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint change register linked to versioned configuration or code, requirements, test evidence, approvals, release records and post-release checks.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents GetConnectors for retrieval and FiEntries for financial posting, providing components for controlled integrations.
AI assistance can draft interface code, mappings and documentation; accounting acceptance and reliable operation require local testing.
The saving and speedup estimates assume available test access and a system owner able to support approved changes.

risks: Generated code can mishandle rounding, periods, retries or accounting dimensions.
An interface can appear successful while only part of a batch was posted.
Broad connector permissions can expose payroll or other unnecessary personal data.
Undocumented custom automation can become dependent on one accountant.
Integration and maintenance costs can exceed the value of a small local time saving.
research_questions: Which current system problems contribute most to close delay, rework or audit adjustments?
Are AFAS test access, connector permissions and technical support available?
Can the proposed solution pass duplicate-run, partial-failure and recovery tests with correct control totals?
Does the measured benefit exceed build, licensing and ongoing maintenance costs?

role.altitude: The accountant becomes the owner of accounting data quality, reconciliation rules and close controls, investigating material exceptions and improving the system that produces trusted actuals.
reach: Controller: coordinate close readiness, maintain control evidence and explain recurring accounting errors.
Bookkeeper: govern complex matching, coding rules and upstream posting quality.
FP&A Analyst: supply earlier provisional actuals, accrual ranges and reliable site cost explanations.
Credit and Collections Officer: resolve receipt-allocation exceptions and improve customer reference quality.
